Calathes's full name is Nicholas William Calathes (Greek: Νικόλαος Γουίλιαμ "Νικ" Καλάθης).
Calathes was born on February 7, 1989.
Calathes is a Greek-American professional basketball player.
AS Monaco is Calathes's current team in the French LNB Pro A and EuroLeague.
Calathes is widely considered one of the best point guards in EuroLeague history.
Calathes played college basketball for the Florida Gators.
Calathes won the EuroLeague title with Panathinaikos in 2011.
Calathes reached another final in 2021 with FC Barcelona.
Calathes is a two-time All-EuroLeague First Team selection.
Calathes holds the EuroLeague all-time assists record.
Calathes also holds the EuroLeague all-time steals record.
Calathes represents the Hellenic national basketball team internationally.
Calathes won a bronze medal at EuroBasket 2009.
Calathes's father started the Orlando Raptors, where he won several AAU Championships.
Calathes attended Lake Howell High School in Winter Park, Florida.
Calathes graduated as the leading high school basketball scorer in Seminole County history.
Calathes played with future Florida Gator Chandler Parsons and future VCU Ram Joey Rodriguez at Lake Howell.
Calathes helped Lake Howell to a 31–3 record and a state championship in 2007.
Calathes accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the University of Florida.
Calathes played for coach Billy Donovan's Florida Gators men's basketball team from 2007 to 2009.
Calathes was considered one of the top play-making guards in college basketball.
Calathes is 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m) tall.
Calathes could play as a point guard, shooting guard, and small forward.
Calathes was a first-team All-Southeastern Conference (SEC) selection in 2009.
Calathes was the only player in the nation to average better than 15.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game in 2009.
Calathes broke Florida school records for assists and assists per game as a freshman (6.1 assists per game) and sophomore (6.4 assists per game).
Calathes ranked third in Florida school history in career assists after two years.
Calathes was the SEC Newcomer of the Year and co-Freshman of the Year in 2008.
Calathes led Florida in scoring and assists.
On May 23, 2009, Calathes announced he would bypass the NBA to play in the Greek Basket League.
Calathes agreed to terms with Panathinaikos Athens for a three-year deal.
The deal paid Calathes around €2.4 million net income.
Calathes was still selected in the second round of the 2009 NBA draft by the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Calathes was then traded to the Dallas Mavericks for a 2010 second-round draft pick and cash.
In his first year with Panathinaikos, Calathes won the Greek League championship.
In his first year with Panathinaikos, Calathes averaged 5.4 points, 2.0 assists, and 2.2 rebounds in 15 minutes per game.
Calathes participated in the Greek Youth All-Star Game (for players age 22 and under).
Calathes scored six points and dished six assists in the Greek Youth All-Star Game.
In 2010, Calathes was voted the third best young player (age 22 and under) in the Greek League.
In the 2010–11 season, Calathes had an average of 7.8 points, 3.2 assists, and 3.1 rebounds in the Greek League.
Calathes participated in the senior men's HEBA Greek All-Star Game.
Calathes replaced Theo Papaloukas (who was out with an injury) in the senior men's HEBA Greek All-Star Game.
Calathes scored 11 points and dished six assists in the senior men's HEBA Greek All-Star Game.
In the EuroLeague 2010–11 playoffs, Calathes scored a career-high 12 points against Barcelona in game 4 of the playoff series.
Barcelona head coach Xavi Pascual said Diamantidis was the MVP of the series, but Calathes was the key player.
Calathes's teammate Ian Vougioukas stated that Calathes played four outstanding games, especially on defense, and was a key for them.
In the 2010–11 EuroLeague semifinal against Montepaschi Siena, Calathes had another good performance.
Calathes scored 17 points, dished two assists to his teammates, and grabbed six rebounds in the 2010–11 EuroLeague semifinal.
In the 2010–11 EuroLeague Final against Maccabi Tel Aviv, Calathes helped Panathinaikos.
Calathes scored four points, recorded six assists, and made two steals in the 2010–11 EuroLeague Final.
In the 2010–11 Greek League playoffs, Calathes had an average of 8.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 3.8 assists per game.
Calathes helped Panathinaikos reach the Greek League Finals.
On July 15, 2015, Panathinaikos announced the signing of Calathes for three years.
The net income of the deal was $7 million dollars.
Calathes set a new personal career-high of 11 assists in a EuroLeague game on October 22 against Karşıyaka Basket.
On March 6, 2016, Calathes won the Greek Cup for the second time with Panathinaikos.
Calathes was named the 2016 Greek League Best Defender.
Calathes won the Greek Cup again with Panathinaikos in 2017.
Calathes also won the Greek championship title.
On July 9, 2020, Calathes signed with FC Barcelona of the Spanish Liga ACB.
Calathes was excluded from the plans of Barcelona coach Šarūnas Jasikevičius for the 2022–23 season.
On August 23, 2022, Calathes signed a two-year contract with Fenerbahçe of the Turkish Basketball Super League.
Calathes helped Fenerbahçe make its return to the EuroLeague Final Four after a five-year break.
On June 17, 2024, Calathes signed a two-year deal with AS Monaco of the French LNB Pro A and the EuroLeague.
Calathes joined his former Panathinaikos teammate Mike James at AS Monaco.
Calathes made his debut with the Greek junior national team at the 2008 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship.
Calathes averaged 11.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 3.7 assists in 22 minutes per game for the Greek junior national team.
Calathes debuted with the Greece men's national basketball team in 2009.
Calathes won a bronze medal at EuroBasket 2009.
Calathes was fifth in steals during the 2009 EuroBasket, averaging 1.6 per game.
Calathes averaged 4.1 points, 2.1 rebounds, and two assists in 17 minutes per game for Greece.
Greece failed to win a medal at the 2010 FIBA World Championship.
Calathes averaged 4.5 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 2.5 assists during the tournament.
Calathes helped Greece finish in sixth place at the EuroBasket 2011.
Calathes averaged 9.2 points and 3.8 assists per game for Greece.
Calathes played at the 2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament with Greece.
Calathes played with Greece at the EuroBasket 2017.
Calathes also played in the 2019 FIBA World Cup qualification.
Calathes has played with the Greece men's national basketball team in 105 games, scoring 851 points for an average of 8.1 points per game.
Calathes was born to a Greek-American father and an Irish-American mother.
Calathes holds dual citizenship with the United States and Greece.
Calathes acquired his Greek passport on June 30, 2008.
Calathes's paternal grandparents emigrated from the Greek island Lemnos.
Calathes's older brother, Pat, is also a professional basketball player.
Calathes's last name in Greek translates as "basket" (καλάθι).
In 2013, Calathes's fiancé, Tiffany, gave birth to their first child.
Calathes has played for multiple teams throughout his career.
